verifications.claim: The last human moon launch was NASA's Apollo 17 mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Apollo 17 — the final mission in the program, which was the last time humans traveled to the moon.'; R3: 'Apollo 17 became the last crewed mission to the Moon'; R5: 'the last humans to visit the Moon'; R6: 'Apollo 17 was the last lunar landing mission.'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple references explicitly state Apollo 17 was the last human/crewed mission to the Moon.

verifications.claim: NASA's Apollo 17 mission launched on December 7, 1972.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'on Dec. 7, 1972'; R3: 'taking place between 7 and 19 December 1972'; R6: 'Dec. 7, 1972; 12:33 a.m. EST'
verifications.reasoning: Exact launch date directly stated in multiple references.

verifications.claim: Astronauts Eugene Cernan and Harrison Schmitt landed in the Taurus-Littrow valley.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'Taurus-Littrow landing site'; R5: 'landed on the Moon in the valley of Taurus-Littrow'; R6: 'lunar landing site was the Taurus-Littrow highlands and valley area.'
verifications.reasoning: References confirm Cernan and Schmitt as landing crew at Taurus-Littrow.

verifications.claim: Eugene Cernan and Harrison Schmitt spent three days on the lunar surface.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'more than three of those on the lunar surface'; R4: 'three days exploring the Taurus-Littrow site'; R5: landing Dec 11 to departure Dec 14; R6: 'lunar surface-stay time was 75 hours'
verifications.reasoning: 75 hours is precisely over three days; references confirm Cernan and Schmitt as surface crew for that duration.

verifications.claim: Eugene Cernan and Harrison Schmitt departed the lunar surface on December 14, 1972.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R5: 'stepped off the lunar surface for the last time on December 14, 1972'; R6: 'The LM ascent stage lifted off the moon at 10:54:37 p.m. Dec. 14.'
verifications.reasoning: Exact departure date for Cernan and Schmitt directly confirmed.

verifications.claim: Eugene Cernan was the last human to walk on the moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'Cernan was the last to leave the lunar surface, and therefore is the most recent person to stand on the Moon'; R4: 'Eugene Cernan, the last man to walk on the moon'
verifications.reasoning: References explicitly identify Cernan as the last person to walk/stand on the Moon.

verifications.claim: Eugene Cernan was the Commander of NASA's Apollo 17 mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'Eugene Cernan as Mission Commander'; R6: 'Eugene A. Cernan, Commander'
verifications.reasoning: Role directly attributed to Cernan in references.

verifications.claim: Harrison Schmitt was the Lunar Module Pilot of NASA's Apollo 17 mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'Harrison H. Schmitt was the lunar module pilot'; R6: 'Harrison H. Schmitt, Lunar Module Pilot'
verifications.reasoning: Role directly attributed to Schmitt in references.

verifications.claim: Ronald Evans was the Command Module Pilot of NASA's Apollo 17 mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'Ronald E. Evans as command module pilot'; R6: 'Ronald E. Evans, Command Module Pilot'
verifications.reasoning: Role directly attributed to Evans in references.

verifications.claim: NASA's Apollo 17 mission was the final mission of the Apollo program.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'the final mission in the program'; R6: 'Apollo 17 was the last lunar landing mission'
verifications.reasoning: References confirm it as the final Apollo lunar mission.

verifications.claim: NASA's Apollo 17 mission featured the longest moonwalks.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'broke many records, including the longest space walk'; R6: 'Three extravehicular activities, or EVAs, lasted a total of 22 hours, four minutes'
verifications.reasoning: References note longest spacewalk/EVA records, synonymous with moonwalks.

verifications.claim: NASA's Apollo 17 mission featured the largest sample collection.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'gathered more geology samples than any other moon mission, bringing 243 pounds'; R3: 'the largest lunar samples brought back to Earth'; R6: 'gathered 110.4 kilograms, or 243 pounds, of material'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple references confirm largest samples returned.

verifications.claim: Robotic missions have landed on the moon since 1972.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.reasoning: No references explicitly mention robotic moon landings post-1972.

verifications.claim: China's Chang'e series have landed on the moon since 1972.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.reasoning: Chang'e mentioned only as future human program, no post-1972 landings noted.

verifications.claim: The NASA Artemis II mission is set for 2026.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R3: 'Artemis 2 just successfully completed its mission - it launched on 1 April 2026'
verifications.reasoning: One reference states launch in 2026 (past tense), but not phrased as 'set for'; others lack specific date.

verifications.claim: The NASA Artemis II mission marks the first crewed mission back to the moon in over 50 years.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'NASA’s Artemis II mission... first launch to the moon in 53 years'; cited snippet: 'NASA's Artemis II will be humanity’s first launch to the moon in 53 years'
verifications.reasoning: Reference directly supports as first crewed lunar mission in over 50 years.
